items.t: Harbour Chines is the "Chines" slope of central Coquitlam served by Como Lake Avenue, adjoining the Chineside sub-area; its boundaries are UNVERIFIED — no City neighbourhood plan boundary for Harbour Chines is stated on a City page in the sources read, and an official City of Coquitlam neighbourhood plan name for Harbour Chines is also UNVERIFIED. Nearby areas: Chineside to the west/south-west, Central Coquitlam to the east, Ranch Park to the south, and the City Centre / Pinetree Way edge to the north-east.

Current listing evidence for the sub-area is detached houses only — a current listing page for the area describes tree-lined streets of detached homes, with most homes on lots of 10,000 square feet or more.

Main roads: Como Lake Avenue serves the Chines area; exact sub-area boundary roads are UNVERIFIED. Como Lake Park is a City park name in City records for central Coquitlam; parks inside Harbour Chines by official name are UNVERIFIED. The nearest hospital is Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border. The nearest library branch is the Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way.

blocks.text: Good to know about Harbour Chines

items.t: Filing a Harbour Chines deal in the wrong city changes the taxes, the bylaws and the school district on paper.
The 33% headline ratio rests on three sales.

The density story here is suites and coach homes, not strata. The SSMUH framework (up to 3 units on lots ≤280 m², up to 4 units under 4,050 m²) is the only multi-unit mechanism operating on Harbour Chines streets, and area listing copy markets the large lots for laneway/coach potential — a sub-area can be densifying and still have zero condos.

No Harbour Chines school catchment is verified yet. No address in this sub-area has a recorded SD43 locator result, and no in-area school is named on a district source read — any listing that states a catchment for a Harbour Chines address as settled fact is ahead of the verified record.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Harbour Chines
Streets, schools and getting around Harbour Chines

items.t: Harbour Chines is a central Coquitlam pocket on the slope above Como Lake Avenue — "chines" being the ravine/valley terrain, and there is no harbour or waterfront in the sub-area despite the name. Its precise boundary roads: UNVERIFIED (no City neighbourhood-plan text for "Harbour Chines" has been located; the name functions as a board/statistical sub-area, not a confirmed City plan area).

Do not merge Chineside: Harbour Chines and Chineside are two separate Coquitlam sub-areas with separate rows in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report. Stats, stock and catchments from one never carry to the other.

Medians are community-level only: Coquitlam "Condos & Townhomes" COMBINED median was $625,000 in September 2026 ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days on market), and the Coquitlam detached median was $1,455,000 — cited exactly as the report states them, never as Harbour Chines figures.

Transit: no station is inside Harbour Chines; the nearest SkyTrain stations are Coquitlam Central and Burquitlam on the Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line); per-route bus numbers for the sub-area: UNVERIFIED.

School names that appear on listing pages for Harbour Chines houses (including Harbour View Elementary and Dr. Charles Best Secondary) are listing copy, not district-verified catchments — run the exact address in the SD43 School Locator.

Parks: Como Lake Park is a City of Coquitlam park name for the central-Coquitlam Como Lake area; whether any part of it sits inside this sub-area: UNVERIFIED — do not market it as in-area without a boundary source.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Harbour Chines

items.t: City zoning and plan — standing corrections applied (Coquitlam): Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 — small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, subdivision minimums 650 m² / 18.5 m width (R-1, R-3) and 465 m² / 12.5 m (R-2). The Interim Official Community Plan — Bylaws 5511/5512, 2026 — was adopted April 27, 2026 and supersedes OCP No. 3479; cite the interim OCP, never 3479.

Presales (REDMA), if any are ever marketed here: a presale buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21), with deposits in trust. No presale is verified in Harbour Chines.

blocks.text: Good to know about Harbour Chines

items.t: The name promises a harbour that does not exist: "Harbour Chines" is a slope-and-ravine name above Como Lake Avenue — there is no waterfront, marina or harbour in the sub-area, and the only "Harbour" townhouse complex a search returns is in Port Coquitlam.
Any page or pitch quoting the 33% without the count is misusing the report.
Two sub-areas share the "Chines" root: Harbour Chines and Chineside are separate SnapStats rows and separate pockets — a comp pulled from Chineside is not a Harbour Chines comp.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Harbour Chines
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established house lots: detached houses on the Como Lake slope under the small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 in Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996, as the research states them. Lot character, only: subdivision minimums are 650 m² with 18.5 m width in R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width in R-2. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are UNVERIFIED until checked parcel by parcel. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules, so property-level septic or well status is UNVERIFIED in the research — confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: parcel-level ALR status for Harbour Chines: UNVERIFIED in the sources read; no ALR percentage split is stated. Check any parcel in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Watercourse position: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks and s.523 covers riparian areas. Lot-level status: UNVERIFIED per lot.

items.t: Nearby areas: Chineside (the adjoining "Chines" sub-area, also Coquitlam), Central Coquitlam to the east, Ranch Park to the south, and the City Centre / Pinetree Way edge to the north-east.

Parks, recreation and library: Como Lake Park is a City park name in City records for central Coquitlam; parks inside Harbour Chines by official name: UNVERIFIED. City Centre Aquatic Complex and Evergreen Cultural Centre are in the City Centre area to the north-east (addresses UNVERIFIED in the research). The nearest library branch is the Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, with the Poirier branch at 575 Poirier Street, plus the Library Link mobile service. Health care: Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody.

Roads and transit: Como Lake Avenue serves the Chines area; exact sub-area boundary roads: UNVERIFIED. The nearest Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations are Coquitlam Central and Burquitlam; bus routes serving Harbour Chines streets: UNVERIFIED. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Schools: SD43 catchments are address-based. In-area SD43 schools for Harbour Chines: UNVERIFIED — no district source read names a school physically inside this sub-area. The nearest master-research locator run (1169 Pinetree Way, returning Glen Elementary, École Maple Creek Middle and Pinetree Secondary) sits at the City Centre edge and is NOT confirmed as a Harbour Chines catchment — no Harbour Chines address-level result is verified, so run the exact address in the SD43 locator. Programs of Choice (French Immersion, Mandarin Bilingual, Montessori) and cross-catchment moves are application / lottery processes, never catchment rights.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Harbour Chines

items.t: Bare-land strata block (for the form — no Harbour Chines bare-land strata plan is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Harbour Chines ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31).

faq.q: What sold in Harbour Chines in September 2026?
faq.a: Detached: 3 solds from 9 listings (33% sales ratio — small sample, only 3 sales); condos & townhomes: 0 solds from 0 listings, so no ratio applies. At the Coquitlam community level the detached median sale price was $1,455,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $625,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Harbour Chines?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 9 houses listed with 3 sold in the month in Harbour Chines. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Harbour Chines a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 33% on too few listings to read as a market type. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: Can Jared show me homes in Harbour Chines?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Harbour Chines at all?
faq.a: None verified. No condo building or townhome complex name was confirmed on a developer or strata source, and the sub-area recorded 0 condos & townhomes listings in September 2026. A buyer set on a condo is, on current evidence, buying at the City Centre / Burquitlam station clusters or in Central Coquitlam — not in Harbour Chines.

faq.q: Is Harbour Chines in Coquitlam or Port Coquitlam — and is it on the water?
faq.a: Coquitlam, and no. SnapStats carries Harbour Chines only under the Coquitlam community; the name is a slope name in central Coquitlam around Como Lake Avenue, with no harbour, waterfront or Port Coquitlam connection on any source read.

faq.q: Is Harbour Place Estates the Harbour Chines condo complex?
faq.a: No — Harbour Place Estates (1872 Harbour Street) is a 1990 townhouse complex in Port Coquitlam. Same word, different city, different sub-area.

faq.q: Is Harbour Chines the same market as Chineside?
faq.a: No — distinct sub-areas, distinct SnapStats rows. In September 2026 Harbour Chines detached sold 3 of 9 while Chineside sold 0 of 7; blending them invents a market neither one had.

faq.q: I found "Harbour Place Estates" townhouses — is that Harbour Chines?
faq.a: No. Harbour Place Estates (1872 Harbour Street) is in Port Coquitlam.

faq.q: Is Harbour Chines in Port Coquitlam or Coquitlam?
Is Harbour Chines the same as Chineside?
faq.a: No — two separate Coquitlam sub-areas with separate SnapStats rows. Never merge their stats or stock.

faq.q: What does "Condos & Townhomes" median mean for Harbour Chines?
faq.a: Nothing sub-area-specific: SnapStats publishes the Coquitlam combined median ($625,000, September 2026) at community level only, and there is no townhome-only figure anywhere in the report. Harbour Chines' own attached row is 0/0.
